# Cold‑Chain Corridor Strategy: Buy Thermal Autonomy, Not Refrigeration

## 1. Strategic Thesis

Three propositions drive every decision below.

**(a) You cannot fix African transit variance — so stop buying reliability and start buying tolerance.** Road condition, customs dwell, port congestion, ferry closures, fuel availability and security incidents will remain high‑variance for the life of this contract. The correct engineering response is not tighter scheduling; it is a thermal system that is *indifferent* to delay up to a defined percentile. Every lane is therefore specified by a **thermal autonomy budget** — hours of guaranteed in‑spec protection at a defined ambient profile — sized against the **P95 exposure time**, never the planned transit time.

**(b) The loss is downstream, not on the trunk.** In most EPI systems the majority of potency loss occurs in static storage at district and facility level and during outreach sessions — and a large share of it is **freeze damage to freeze‑sensitive antigens** (DTP‑containing pentavalent, HepB, HPV, IPV, PCV), not heat damage. A strategy that optimises the port‑to‑capital leg and hands over a pallet at the central medical store will look excellent on our KPIs and still destroy vaccine. Investment must be deliberately asymmetric toward the last 200 km.

**(c) Centralise judgement, federate execution.** One control tower, one thermal data model, one excursion‑adjudication authority; locally federated fleets, agents, and ministry interfaces. Same logic as any corridor business: the reusable core is the asset.

**Organising metric — Cost per Dose Delivered In‑Spec (CPDDI):**

> **CPDDI = (freight + equipment amortisation & recovery cost + energy + monitoring + customs/handling + last‑mile + insurance + expected value of doses lost + carrying cost of buffer stock + CCE maintenance) ÷ doses arriving and remaining usable at point of administration**

Note the denominator: *usable at point of administration*, not *delivered to consignee*. Contract on this and the incentives align. Freight rate per tonne‑km is a vanity number; it is typically a minority of CPDDI.

---

## 2. Corridor Segmentation

Score every lane on two axes.

**Axis A — Thermal difficulty:** product temperature class (−70/−20/+2–8/CTC‑eligible), freeze sensitivity, P95 exposure hours (transit + dwell + last mile), ambient profile (Sahel dry season vs. coastal humid), availability of re‑icing/swap points, reliability of grid power at intermediate nodes.

**Axis B — Institutional & infrastructure friction:** customs dwell variance, road/seasonal closure risk, security, NRA and import‑permit predictability, MoH/EPI absorptive capacity, quality of subnational cold chain equipment (CCE), payment and data discipline.

| Quadrant | Profile | Posture | Equipment & custody model |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anchor** | Moderate thermal difficulty, workable institutions (Kenya, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, coastal Tanzania) | Own end‑to‑end to point of administration | Owned/leased reefer trunk + PCM passive inner packaging; own subnational hubs; direct facility delivery |
| **Strategic‑hard** | High volume or high difficulty but strategically essential (Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, DRC‑east, Côte d'Ivoire) | Invest, but sequence and de‑risk | Hybrid: our thermal system, local transport partners; custody transfer at subnational store initially, pushed downstream as control matures |
| **Fragile** | Sahel, South Sudan, Chad, conflict‑affected zones | Never own the last mile | Long‑autonomy passive only; hand to UNICEF/WFP/ICRC/MoH at a secure forward node; contractual custody transfer *upstream* |
| **Marginal** | Low volume, high friction, no strategic anchor | Serve opportunistically or decline | Consolidate into a neighbour's route or subcontract; refuse standalone SLAs |

**Discipline:** review quarterly against a published CPDDI hurdle. Any lane exceeding hurdle CPDDI or falling below the in‑spec delivery floor for two consecutive quarters enters a 90‑day remediation (re‑spec equipment, change partner, re‑route, renegotiate custody point) and is then restructured or handed back. Without a hard rule, a distribution network accumulates heroic, unprofitable lanes that consume the control tower's attention.

---

## 3. Network Architecture: Two Thermal Hubs, Forward Nodes, Spoke‑Light

Do not replicate full capability in every country.

**Hub West — Tema/Accra.** Deep‑water port, comparatively predictable customs and power, ECOWAS access, credible air link via Kotoka. Functions: bonded temperature‑controlled receiving, ULT and 2–8°C bulk storage, PCM conditioning plant, shipper refurbishment/reverse‑log
